title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed letter from Barry Mazur, signed 'Barry', to Grothendieck ('Shurik'). It is filed with the Teichmüller notes and is presumably from 1981. Mazur answers a list of questions Grothendieck had sent. He is planning a visit to IHES: Deligne is free at the end of May or start of June, Mazur lectures on Mondays, and he asks whether Grothendieck wants a room at the Ormaille residence.

The questions are clearly aimed at the Nielsen realization problem. Let Γ be a finite subgroup of the Teichmüller (mapping class) group Mod(S) = Diff⁺(S)/Diff₀(S). Its preimage E in Diff⁺(S) is an extension 1 → Diff₀(S) → E → Γ → 1. By Earle–Eells, Diff₀(S) is contractible. If such an extension always splits, Γ lifts to an actual group of diffeomorphisms and hence acts on some algebraic curve.

So Grothendieck's Question (a) must be: does every extension of a finite group by a contractible group split? Question (b): can a contractible group have elements of finite order? The 'cone' question asks whether a finite-group action on a ball is controlled by its behaviour on the boundary (cone off the boundary action). The last question is about finite subgroups of the Teichmüller group directly.

Mazur's answers:
(a) 'No', via an example of Deligne. H = ⟨x, y | x³ = y³ = 1, [x, y] central⟩, with C = ⟨[x, y]⟩ claimed infinite cyclic, so 1 → C → H → Γ = (Z/3)² → 1. C is identified with the centre Z of G̃, the universal cover of SL₂R. A pushout E = (G̃ × H)/C then gives 1 → G̃ → E → Γ → 1, claimed non-split.
(b) 'Yes' for Lie groups, unknown beyond. The marginal note reads '(∞-dim'l)': it is unknown whether an infinite-dimensional contractible group can have torsion.
(Cone) Negative: there is a Bing-type involution of B³ whose fixed set on S² is a tame circle but whose fixed set in the interior is wild.
(Teichmüller) Related to recent work of Thurston; the full story is not yet known.

The reverse page (after 't.s.v.p.') adds a handwritten report from Siebenmann and 'Kravitz', i.e. S. Kravetz. Realization of all finite subgroups is open, but known for solvable groups (Fenchel) and for genus 2. Kerckhoff settled the general case in 1983.
errors: H as presented is finite, not an extension with infinite cyclic kernel. If z = [x, y] is central, the commutator is bilinear, so z³ = [x³, y] = 1. Thus C ≅ Z/3 and H is the Heisenberg group of order 27, so C cannot be identified with the centre Z of G̃.

Even with a correct central extension 1 → Z → H → Γ → 1, the pushout E = (G̃ × H)/Z always splits. G̃ contains a one-parameter subgroup R ⊃ Z(G̃) ≅ Z. The subgroup (R × H)/Z ⊂ E is a central extension of finite Γ by R, which splits because H²(Γ, R) = 0.

More generally, every extension of a finite group by a connected contractible Lie group G splits. E is a Lie group with finitely many components, so it has a maximal compact subgroup K that meets every component. K ∩ G is a compact subgroup of G, hence trivial, so K ≅ Γ is a section. The reported answer 'no' to (a) is therefore wrong at least in the Lie setting; it is inconsistent with the letter's own 'yes for Lie groups' to (b).

Beyond Lie groups, the 'unknown' in (b) was already settled. Hartman–Mycielski groups (1958), e.g. L⁰([0,1], Z/2) in measure topology, are contractible topological groups in which every element has order 2. So contractible groups can have torsion.

ideas.what: Reformulating Nielsen realization as splitting of extensions of finite groups by the contractible group Diff₀(S)
ideas.modern_name: Nielsen realization problem / lifting finite subgroups of Mod(S) to Diff(S)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen, Fenchel (solvable case), Kerckhoff 1983 (general); Earle–Eells for contractibility of Diff₀
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller towers and finite subgroups but not, as far as I know, this splitting formulation

ideas.what: Deligne's purported non-split extension of (Z/3)² by the universal cover of SL₂R
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of a central extension along Z → Z(G̃)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unpublished; attributed to Deligne in this letter

ideas.what: Contractible Lie groups have no torsion
ideas.modern_name: Cartan–Iwasawa–Malcev: G is homotopy equivalent to its maximal compact subgroup

ideas.what: Involution of B³ with tame boundary fixed circle but wild interior fixed set
State of Nielsen realization c. 1981: open in general; solvable groups and genus 2 known

missed.claim: The archive records that Deligne's counterexample to 'extensions of finite groups by contractible groups split', as relayed by Mazur, is flawed. H is finite, and any such central pushout into the universal cover of SL₂R splits. Over Lie groups the true answer is yes, via maximal compact subgroups. This shows Grothendieck receiving a mistaken negative answer to a question that, in the Lie case, has a positive answer.
missed.quote: The answer to Question (a) seems to be no. Here is a sketch of an example that Deligne made up.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This matters historically: it documents Grothendieck's 1981 homotopy/group-extension approach to Nielsen realization and the misinformation he received. Mathematically, the question is mostly settled: Kerckhoff 1983 for Diff, and Hartman–Mycielski-type groups show torsion in contractible groups.

missed.claim: Grothendieck framed finite subgroups of the Teichmüller group as a splitting question for extensions by a contractible structure group. This is an early formulation in the spirit of later work on lifting problems Mod(S) → Diff(S) and Homeo(S).
missed.quote: The question about finite subgroups of the Teichmuller group seems to be related to recent work of Thurston
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a modest historical link between the 'Teichmülleries' notes and the Nielsen realization and Morita-type lifting literature. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter rather than Grothendieck's own mathematics. Its interest is historical: it shows his Nielsen-realization-style questions in 1981 and a garbled or incorrect counterexample attributed to Deligne. Nothing substantive is missing from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The marginal insertion after 'contractible group' reads '(∞-dim'l)' (infinite-dimensional), not '(so-lid)'.
The closing reads 'Best, et à bientôt / Barry'; the author is evidently Barry Mazur. '(t.s.v.p.)' replaces a crossed-out 'Please'.
The bottom row of the diagram ends with '→ 0' as typed or drawn (an inconsistency with '→ 1' in the top row).
'Kravitz' on the next page is presumably S. Kravetz.
